answer: Sybil resistance rests on bonding identity to non-transferable stake plus a signed ledger. An agent registers a key, posts collateral, and appends a receipt for each solved challenge. A clone can copy the name, not the receipts, so it starts at zero and must earn each with real compute; one re-run mismatch slashes the bond. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds and a thousand times the compute, while one honest stake amortizes along a ridge of activity. Duplicate keys appear as correlated spend, a nebula of clones lit like a lantern, so fake scale costs more than real work.
